# Finite simple groups are generated by two elements

This repository contains a Lean 4 proof that every finite simple group is generated by two elements, using [AxiomMath/CFSG](https://github.com/AxiomMath/CFSG)'s proof of the classification of finite simple groups.

[`Comparator/Solution.lean`](Comparator/Solution.lean) proves two theorems, one conditional and one unconditional.

The conditional theorem assumes the classification, stated as TauCeti's `ClassificationStatement` (every finite simple group is isomorphic to one on TauCeti's list).

```lean
theorem CFSGCorollary.exists_closure_pair_eq_top_of_classification
    (hCFSG : TauCeti.ClassificationStatement.{0}) (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G]
    [IsSimpleGroup G] : ∃ a b : G, Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤
```

The unconditional theorem applies the conditional theorem to CFSG's proof of the classification, `CFSG.Certified.classification_finite_simple_groups`.

```lean
theorem CFSGCorollary.exists_closure_pair_eq_top (G : Type u) [Group G] [Finite G]
    [IsSimpleGroup G] : ∃ a b : G, Subgroup.closure {a, b} = ⊤
```

- Most of the work is in the `CFSGCorollary` library, which proves that every group on TauCeti's list (cyclic of prime order, alternating, of Lie type, or one of the 26 sporadic groups) is generated by two elements.
- Both theorems depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`.
- The development consists of ~18,600 lines of Lean, excluding dependencies.

## Built on

- **[R. Steinberg, *Generators for simple groups*](https://doi.org/10.4153/CJM-1962-018-0)**, Canad. J. Math. 14 (1962) 277–283: the groups of Lie type
- **[AxiomMath/CFSG](https://github.com/AxiomMath/CFSG)**: the classification, and models of the groups on the list, identified with TauCeti's carriers
- **[TauCeti](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti)**: the classification statement and the list
- **[Mathlib](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4)**

## The proof

The classification gives `G ≃* i.Group` for an index `i` on TauCeti's list, and two-generation transfers along isomorphisms, so it suffices to treat each family.

- **Cyclic**: generated by one element.
- **Alternating**: a 3-cycle and an `n`- or `(n - 1)`-cycle generate a primitive group containing a 3-cycle, hence the alternating group by Jordan's theorem (Mathlib).
- **Sporadic**: CFSG gives each as the closure of two permutations or the units of a monoid generated by two matrices; for the Monster, two explicit products of the generators of TauCeti's Coxeter-type presentation suffice.
- **Lie type**: Steinberg's Lemmas 3.9, 3.10 and 3.12, proved once for abstract root group systems and instantiated on CFSG's models: `SL`, `Sp`, `Spin` and the adjoint exceptional groups (untwisted); `SU`, minus-type `Spin`, ³D₄, ²E₆, Suzuki, and small and large Ree groups (twisted). The Tits group is the closure of two permutations.

| Directory | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `CFSGCorollary/TwoGenerated` | two-generation and its transfer along isomorphisms and surjections |
| `CFSGCorollary/Cyclic.lean`, `Alternating`, `Sporadic` | cyclic, alternating and sporadic groups |
| `CFSGCorollary/LieType/Steinberg` | Steinberg's Lemmas 3.9–3.12 for root group systems |
| `CFSGCorollary/LieType/LambdaRootGroup` | the same, for root groups coordinatized over a finite field (twisted groups) |
| `CFSGCorollary/LieType/Chevalley` | untwisted groups on CFSG's models: root computations (`Roots`) and generation (`Generation`) per Cartan type |
| `CFSGCorollary/LieType/Twisted` | ²A, ²D, ³D₄, ²E₆, Suzuki, small and large Ree groups |
| `CFSGCorollary/CFSGIndex.lean` | every group on TauCeti's list is two-generated |
| `Checks` | checks that the conditional theorem avoids the classification proof |
| `Comparator/Solution.lean` | both theorems |
| `Comparator/Challenge.lean` | the statements, for comparator |

## Build

The build uses Lean `v4.35.0-rc3`. Mathlib and TauCeti are pinned to the revisions CFSG uses.

CFSG publishes prebuilt files for Linux x86_64 only, and they take about 230 GB of disk. To download them, along with Mathlib's and TauCeti's, and build:

```sh
ulimit -s 1048576
export RUST_MIN_STACK=1073741824 LAKE_ARTIFACT_CACHE=true
curl -fsSLO https://cfsg-downloads.axiommath.workers.dev/lake/lake-cache-get-fast.sh
bash lake-cache-get-fast.sh .
lake build
```

On other platforms, Lake compiles the parts of CFSG it needs from source.

If you have built any Mathlib module yourself with this toolchain, the downloaded files won't match and Lake will rebuild CFSG from source. To avoid this, start with an empty Lake cache (`~/.elan/toolchains/<toolchain>/lake/cache`) and `.lake` directory.

The build prints the axioms each theorem depends on, and two expected `sorry` warnings from `Comparator/Challenge.lean`. To build only the library, run `lake build CFSGCorollary`. It doesn't import CFSG's proof of the classification.

[`comparator.json`](comparator.json) lists both theorems, but neither has been checked with comparator (due to time constraints).
